citation: State cybersecurity exhibit (CT-S) (contract; Fla. Stat. 282.318(4)(h) requires the exhibit)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed security incident affecting agency systems, sites, or data
notify: Agency information security manager and contract manager

citation: GSA BTTRG v3.0 section 1.6.1 and CT-F statement of work
trigger: Potential cyber incident involving GSA BMC systems, GSA data (including CUI drawings), or credentials of company staff with GSA access
notify: GSA IT (per contract contact list) and the GSA contracting officer's representative
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if GSA systems, data, or staff credentials may be involved

obligation: County's own report to the state (customer duty)
trigger: County determines a ransomware incident or a severity level 3-5 cybersecurity incident
deadline: County reports no later than 48 hours after discovery (12 hours for ransomware); the company's notice must arrive well before that
notify: County reports to the Cybersecurity Operations Center, FDLE Cybercrime Office, and the sheriff; the company supplies facts
applies_at_this_tier: Customer duty - company supports with facts and timeline

trigger: Remediation of a cybersecurity or ransomware incident
deadline: County submits within 1 week after remediation
notify: Florida Digital Service (by the county); company supplies input

trigger: Agency determines a ransomware incident or a severity level 3-5 cybersecurity incident
deadline: Agency reports no later than 48 hours after discovery (12 hours for ransomware)
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center and FDLE Cybercrime Office (by the agency); company supplies facts

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the customer
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains that holds customer personal information (for example cardholder names with face templates, which are likely biometric data under 501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VI) and 501.702; counsel confirms whether badge credential numbers count)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (contracts require 24 hours, which comes first)
notify: The state agency or county (the entity that gives notice to individuals); provide all information it needs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company is a third-party agent; counsel confirms whether the county is a governmental entity under 501.171(1)(f)

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (company data)
trigger: Breach of the company's own personal information (employees, for example SSNs or background check data)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company is a covered entity for its own data

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (15 more days for individual notice with written good cause)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500+ Florida residents (as covered entity; for customer data the customer notifies)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
Affected cardholders or employees who reside outside Florida
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law

obligation: Covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment found
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Incident investigation identifies covered equipment used as a substantial or essential component
deadline: Within one business day of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered article identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.

citation: FAR 52.204-30(c)(3)-(4); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation

deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days.
